links.outcome: Workload and physical strain: secondary-monitor (Cloud) vs overlay on main surgical monitor (Edge)
links.effect: Cloud secondary monitor had higher NASA-TLX physical (mean diff 17.33, p=0.0004) and frustration (mean diff 14.33, p=0.0036). Strain reported by 60% with Cloud vs 6.7% with Edge. Neck strain significantly greater with Cloud (p=0.0067).
links.quote: Significant mean differences between Cloud and Edge were found in the “physical” (mean difference = 17.33, SD = 14.38, paired t -test, t (14) = 4.670, p value = 0.0004) and “frustration” subcategories (mean difference = 14.33, SD = 15.91, paired t -test, t (14) = 3.489, p value = 0.0036).

links.outcome: Deployment task completion and interface usability issues with representative end users
links.effect: Task completion median 100% Cloud vs 80% Edge (p=2.16×10−5). SUS 65.33 vs 69.67, not significant. Most frequent Edge improvement suggestions concerned the interface (16).
links.quote: Participants achieved a higher completion rate for AI deployment tasks when using Cloud (median 100%, IQR 100–100%) compared to Edge (median 80%, IQR 80–80%).

links.outcome: Estimated operational carbon emissions of cloud versus edge deployment
links.effect: Cloud emitted ~26.22 g CO 2 e every hour during inference, versus 6.84 g CO 2 e for Edge; idle Edge emissions were 3.8 g CO 2 e every hour.
links.quote: Given that Cloud consumes roughly 0.69 kWh of electricity per hour when running AI models, it emits ~26.22 g CO 2 e every hour.

links.outcome: Physical workload and frustration associated with AI deployment configurations

links.outcome: End-user completion of AI deployment tasks
links.effect: Median task completion was 100% (IQR 100–100%) with Cloud versus 80% (IQR 80–80%) with Edge; median difference 20%, p = 2.16 × 10 −5.
links.quote: Participants achieved a higher completion rate for AI deployment tasks when using Cloud (median 100%, IQR 100–100%) compared to Edge (median 80%, IQR 80–80%).

links.outcome: Physical strain with integrated surgical-monitor versus separate-laptop AI displays
links.effect: Strain was reported by 60% with Cloud’s separate laptop versus 6.7% with Edge’s integrated monitor; neck strain median difference was 1.00 (IQR = 0.00–3.00, p = 0.0067).
links.quote: Most participants reported strain in one or more body parts when using AI with Cloud (60%), whereas only one participant reported strain for AI deployment with Edge (6.7%).
